identity.title: ALMA Observations of the Molecular Gas in the Elliptical Galaxy NGC 3557

paper_type_evidence.quote: We present the results of CO interferometric observations of the southern elliptical galaxy NGC 3557 with ALMA.

findings_qualitative.value: CO gas concentrated within ~250 pc, rotating along same axis as stars and dust; radio jet not perpendicular to dust ring

evidence.quote: The radio jet does not appear to be oriented perpendicularly to the nuclear dust ring nor along the stellar rotation axis.

claims.hypothesis: Is the molecular gas mass of NGC 3557 as high as single-dish values suggest?
claims.experiment: ALMA CO(1-0) and CO(2-1) fluxes compared with APEX-based values
claims.result: MH2 = 9.0e7 Msun versus log MH2=9.02 from single-dish
claims.finding: Single-dish value is spurious (standing waves); ALMA mass more plausible

evidence.quote: Based on all this evidence, we conclude that our value for the molecular gas mass in NGC 3557 is more plausible

claims.hypothesis: Does the gas rotate organized along stellar and dust axes?
claims.result: Consistent rotation, inclination 51 deg, PA 232 deg
claims.finding: Bulk rotation present with kinematic horns as departures

evidence.quote: the data for each CO line independently suggests the presence of bulk rotation of the molecular gas in this object

claims.hypothesis: Is the gas disk gravitationally unstable?
claims.experiment: Surface density vs critical density profile
claims.result: Surface density below critical at all radii

evidence.quote: The origin of these high values is not known, but may be related to the interaction of the molecular gas with the radio jet plasma.
